ALRT-0038.investigation_focus: Establish whether the observed activity is explainable against the customer's own baseline and the programme baseline, and whether verification evidence supports activity at this level.
checklist: Compare observed activity against the customer baseline and the programme baseline separately.
Confirm whether KYB and beneficial-owner verification are complete.
Review source-of-funds evidence for activity at this level.
Check whether prior alerts show a developing pattern.
ALRT-0038.escalation_guidance: Suggest escalation for analyst decision where verification evidence is incomplete or the activity is unexplained against both baselines.
ALRT-0038.ai_boundaries: Do not state that the activity is suspicious or that the rule fired correctly. Recommend investigation focus only.

ALRT-0050.investigation_focus: Establish which jurisdictions the activity touches, whether that exposure is consistent with the customer's stated business, and whether the programme treats those jurisdictions as elevated risk.

ALRT-0074.investigation_focus: Establish the counterparty concentration, whether counterparties are newly seen, and whether the commercial relationship is explainable.

ALRT-0085.investigation_focus: Establish the decline and channel pattern behind the alert. Card identity is out of scope: the investigation works from transaction-level indicators only.
checklist: Review the decline pattern against normal activity for this customer.
Compare card-present and card-not-present volumes.
Check whether declines cluster in time, category or geography.
ALRT-0085.escalation_guidance: Suggest escalation where the decline pattern is concentrated and unexplained by ordinary retry behaviour.
ALRT-0085.ai_boundaries: Do not conclude fraud. Do not recommend restricting or blocking a card. No card identifiers are available to this investigation.

ALRT-0090.investigation_focus: Establish whether repeated failures have an ordinary operational explanation or indicate a pattern requiring review.
checklist: Separate transaction failures from top-up failures.
Check whether failures concentrate on one funding source or counterparty.
Consider ordinary operational causes such as expired instruments or retries.
ALRT-0090.escalation_guidance: Suggest escalation only where the failure pattern is not explained by ordinary operational causes.
ALRT-0090.ai_boundaries: Do not conclude that failures indicate testing or illicit activity.

unusual_transaction_velocity.description: Transaction activity has risen sharply against the customer's own recent norm.
unusual_transaction_velocity.purpose: Give the analyst both baselines, the verification position and prior alert history, so the rise can be judged as explained or unexplained. The playbook does not assess whether the upstream rule should have fired.

unusual_topup_pattern.description: Inbound top-up volume, frequency or funding spread has changed materially.
unusual_topup_pattern.purpose: Assemble top-up behaviour, funding spread and any current customer impact so the analyst can see at once whether funds are held and what evidence is outstanding.

high_risk_geography_exposure.description: Activity touches jurisdictions the programme treats as elevated risk.
high_risk_geography_exposure.purpose: Show which jurisdictions carry the exposure and whether that fits the customer's stated business, using the programme's own elevated-risk list rather than any external classification.

high_risk_merchant_category.description: Spend is concentrated in merchant categories the programme monitors.
high_risk_merchant_category.purpose: Identify which monitored categories drive the alert and whether the pattern is consistent with the customer's stated industry.

repeated_failed_kyb_kyc_checks.description: Verification checks have failed or remain outstanding for this customer.
repeated_failed_kyb_kyc_checks.purpose: Set out what verification was attempted, what failed and what is outstanding, so the analyst can decide what to request rather than re-deriving the file history.

sanctions_pep_screening_review_required.description: Upstream screening produced a possible match requiring manual analyst review.
sanctions_pep_screening_review_required.purpose: Present the screening context verbatim and assemble identifying detail for the sanctions analyst. The match itself is never assessed here.

linked_party_or_counterparty_review.description: Counterparty activity is concentrated, newly seen, or shared across customers.
linked_party_or_counterparty_review.purpose: Quantify counterparty concentration and overlap so the analyst can distinguish an ordinary common supplier from a linked-party concern.

possible_account_misuse.description: Account usage diverges from the expected profile for this customer and programme.
possible_account_misuse.purpose: Compare usage against the customer's own baseline and stated business, and surface third-party-use indicators such as counterparty spread and failure rate.

possible_card_misuse.description: Decline and channel patterns are inconsistent with ordinary card usage.
possible_card_misuse.purpose: Characterise the decline and channel pattern from transaction-shape evidence alone, since no card identifier is available to this POC.

repeated_failed_transaction_or_topup_pat.description: Repeated transaction or top-up failures have occurred within a short window.
repeated_failed_transaction_or_topup_pat.purpose: Separate transaction failures from top-up failures and surface whether an ordinary operational cause explains the pattern.

repeated_screening_review.purpose: Group repeated screening review flags within one programme so they can be routed to a sanctions analyst together, with the queue position visible.
repeated_screening_review.interpretation_guidance: A concentration of screening reviews in one programme may reflect the customer population, the screening configuration, or name-matching characteristics of a jurisdiction. None of those is assessed here. The cluster is a routing and workload view over reviews that each remain individually owned.
analyst_guidance: Route the grouped reviews to a sanctions analyst under the approved process.
Note how many member alerts are still awaiting manual confirmation.
Review each member alert individually; screening decisions are per customer.
boundaries: A cluster is a grouping. It establishes a pattern, never wrongdoing.
The cluster assesses no match, confirms no match and dismisses no match.
No sanctions or PEP decision is made at cluster level.
Grouping must never be read as corroboration between unrelated screening matches.

repeated_topup.purpose: Surface repeated top-up review delays concentrated in one programme, where the operational effect on customers may be wider than any single alert shows.
repeated_topup.interpretation_guidance: Repeated top-up alerts in one programme often indicate a funding pattern common to that programme's customers rather than individual behaviour. Because top-up review can leave funds unavailable, a concentration here has a customer-impact dimension that other clusters do not.
analyst_guidance: Determine whether the pattern is customer-specific, programme-level or rule-configuration related.
Check how many member alerts carry a current customer impact such as a delayed top-up.
Review funding-source spread across the member customers.
Treat any customer communication as a separate human-owned workflow.
boundaries: A cluster is a grouping. It establishes a pattern, never wrongdoing.
No customer-facing wording, suspicion reasoning or notice may be drafted here.
The cluster does not release, hold or otherwise affect funds.
The cluster does not change any member alert's own category.

repeated_velocity.purpose: Show the analyst that several velocity alerts in one programme, close together in time, may represent one reviewable pattern rather than several unrelated investigations.
repeated_velocity.interpretation_guidance: A concentration of velocity alerts within one programme has three ordinary explanations before any adverse one: a segment of customers behaving similarly, a baseline that no longer reflects the programme's normal activity, or a rule threshold tuned for a different population. The cluster exists to make that question askable at programme level; it does not answer it.
analyst_guidance: Establish whether the alerts share customers or are spread across many.
Compare the programme baseline against the activity now being seen.
Consider whether rule configuration rather than customer behaviour explains the volume.
Review the individual investigations; the cluster does not replace them.
boundaries: A cluster is a grouping. It establishes a pattern, never wrongdoing.
The cluster does not change any member alert's own category.
The cluster does not produce an insufficient-evidence outcome; that is an individual-alert concept only.
Membership must not be presented to a customer or used as evidence of suspicion.

shared_counterparty_mcc.purpose: Group alerts that share a counterparty or merchant-category context, including across different programmes, so a relationship invisible in any single alert becomes reviewable.
shared_counterparty_mcc.interpretation_guidance: This is the only cluster that deliberately crosses programme boundaries, and it is the one most easily over-read. Unrelated customers commonly share a legitimate supplier, acquirer or advertising platform. Grouping establishes that a shared context exists; it says nothing about why.
analyst_guidance: Identify the shared counterparty or category and its share of each customer's activity.
Establish whether it is a plausible common supplier for the industries involved.
Check whether the member customers have any other connection.
Note that members may sit in different programmes; that is expected here.
boundaries: A cluster is a grouping. It establishes a pattern, never wrongdoing.
Shared counterparties must not be described as evidence of connection for illicit purposes.
The cluster does not change any member alert's own category.

global_ai_boundaries.note: These boundaries are global. Each playbook's own ai_boundaries field adds domain-specific restrictions on top of them and never relaxes them.
model_may: interpret evidence that was actually fetched
summarise the evidence pack
explain the pattern the evidence shows
produce an internal analyst rationale
recommend one outcome from the playbook's allowed_outcomes
recommend insufficient evidence where required evidence is MISSING
model_must_not: fill a MISSING field with an assumption
state or imply that evidence exists when it is MISSING
invent customer, programme, transaction or screening information
recommend an outcome outside the playbook's allowed_outcomes
change, override or modify approved policy or configuration
take prohibited external actions or act outside the approved workflow
screening_specific: must not confirm a possible match as a confirmed match
must not dismiss a possible match as cleared
must not make a final sanctions or PEP decision
must not infer anything from the confidence band beyond reporting its value
global_ai_boundaries.outcome_contract: The model recommends. The analyst confirms. A recommended outcome is never a decision and is never final.
